summary.oneLiner: JG Chemicals delivered record FY26 financials driven by robust tire demand and GST-led auto revival, with Dahej capacity expansion and recycled rubber R&D creating multi-year growth visibility; margin resilience despite March raw material spikes confirms pricing power and supply chain dominance, positioning JG as the indispensable zinc solutions partner for global tire and emerging ceramic markets.

one-line thesis: JG Chemicals delivered record FY26 financials driven by robust tire demand and GST-led auto revival, with Dahej capacity expansion and recycled rubber R&D creating multi-year growth visibility; margin resilience despite March raw material spikes confirms pricing power and supply chain dominance, positioning JG as the indispensable zinc solutions partner for global tire and emerging ceramic markets.
financial scorecard: revenue: +27.6% YoY to INR286.2cr (Q4); EBITDA: +27.6% YoY to INR26.8cr (Q4), margin 9.4% (Q4), 10.1% (FY26) — March cost spike suppressed margin; PAT: +27.6% YoY to INR18.9cr (Q4), INR68.6cr (FY26); order book: not disclosed; net debt: net cash position implied by internal accruals funding INR100cr Dahej capex
guidance: revenue growth: double-digit volume growth expected in FY27; margin: 10-11% baseline, targeting 13-14% with higher-value products; order inflow: strong visibility from tire capex (INR20,000cr over 3 yrs); capex/commissioning: Dahej Phase 1 commissioning H1FY27, brownfield debottlenecking at Naidupeta by Dec26, total capex INR100cr from internal accruals
segment / subsidiary detail: Zinc oxide: 77% utilization (can scale to 87%); Zinc sulphate: 60% utilization; Export mix: 10-15%; Non-rubber demand: ceramics (targeted via Dahej), pharma, electronics, agri; Dahej product mix: 30-35% ceramics, 30-35% tire, rest non-rubber
growth verticals / optionality: Recycled rubber intermediates (pilot validated, commercial project in pipeline); ceramic market entry via Dahej (near Morbi hub); non-rubber share expansion (targeting 30%+ of revenue); potential eastern capacity expansion
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 9.4% in Q4 suppressed by March energy cost spike (doubled) and spot zinc dross procurement (LME surge); pricing fully passed on from April 1, 2026; inventory gains from Q3-Q1 zinc price rise partially offset by March cost shock; baseline margin 10-11%, target 13-14% with premium grades
capex / expansion: INR100cr for Dahej Phase 1 (commissioning H1FY27); brownfield debottlenecking at Naidupeta (completed by Dec26); solar Phase 1 commissioned in FY26; future capex to be funded internally; Dahej Phase 2 to be evaluated by FY29
capital allocation: 100% capex funded by internal accruals; no debt used; prioritizing capacity expansion over buybacks/dividends; sustainability investments (solar, recycling) embedded in capex
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical raw material disruption (mitigated by JG’s supplier dominance); ceramic market adoption speed; zinc price volatility (absorbed via FIFO inventory); execution delay in Dahej Phase 1
management quality / tone: Highly bullish; confident in demand sustainability; frames crises as competitive differentiators; emphasizes customer intimacy, scale, and ESG alignment; tone on recycled rubber project is 'gung-ho'
non-obvious takeaways: JG’s IATF/WHO certifications are de facto barriers to entry — no global competitor matches this; Dahej’s proximity to ceramic hub (Morbi) is a strategic play to capture unpenetrated $1B+ market; recycled rubber project could become a $500cr+ revenue stream by FY30; inventory gains are retained, not passed on — a hidden margin accelerator

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Incorporated in 1975 starting with a ~600 MTPA plant in Kolkata, JGCL is described as the largest manufacturer of Zinc Oxide in India with ~31% market share (as on March 30, 2025), amongst the top 5 manufacturers globally and the largest in Asia (deck footnote: 'Excluding China').
- Described as the largest zinc recycling company, with strong R&D and in-house developed recycling technology for various forms of zinc waste/scrap; it serves 200+ domestic customers and 50+ global customers in more than 10 countries with 90%+ repeat customers.
- Tyre-customer reach is stated two ways in the deck: one slide says '9/10 Global tyre manufacturers served' and 'Top 15 Indian tyre manufacturers served', while the Key Strengths slide says '9 out of Top 10 global and Top 11 domestic Tyre manufacturers are our customers'.
- High entry barriers claimed on three fronts: large tyre accounts take on average 4-5 years minimum to approve a new vendor; a global zinc-scrap sourcing network takes decades of relationships to build; and licences (IATF, WHO GMP, US/British/European Pharma, Indian Pharmacopeia) require stringent systems and capex.
- 'No China Threat' — the deck argues zinc oxide prices are determined by zinc prices on the LME, so China has no competitive edge exporting to India. Over 95% of sales are direct to end customers.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Tyre industry capex] Per recent ATMA reports cited in the deck, an estimated capex of about INR 25,000 crore has been announced by Indian tyre majors, with approx. 25% of tyres produced in India now exported.
- [Auto demand] Per ATMA, Q1 FY27 saw volume growth across major vehicle categories: PV +26.6% YoY, 2W +16.58% YoY, CV +16.48% YoY, 3W +11.32% YoY.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoters 70.99%, Public 22.79%, FII 3.21%, AIF 2.11%, DII 0.89%; marquee shareholders listed are Massachusetts Institute of Technology 2.62%, Carnelian Structural Shift Fund 1.69%, CTL Trusteeship Limited 1.24% and SBI General Insurance Company Limited 0.89%.
- [Future strategy] Stated growth strategies are: expand product portfolio, deeper penetration in domestic markets, diversify customer applications in end-user industries, ramp-up of the zinc sulphate business, and expansion to new geographies.
- [Geography] Geographical presence listed as India, Australia, other SAARC countries, Thailand and Europe, with a slide annotation reading 'Constitutes 99.25% of total exports from India' whose subject is ambiguous in the extract.
